proof.criterion: Review round 3, finding 1: backfillIndex writes the record of an older build's live claim, which moves the revision the claimant's outcome write is compare-and-set against, so the claimant's answer is lost and the delivery is asked for a second time once the claim ends. decide's live-claim branch already avoided exactly this.
proof.surface: The sweep against a real nats-server over a bucket in the state a mixed deploy leaves: an older build's claim live (in_flight, a claimed_at inside the deadline, no pending) while the back-fill runs, with the claimant then writing its outcome over the revision it claimed at.
proof.observed: Passes at 30ceb42013e1. The back-fill writes the entry the claim's end is owed and no record, so the record keeps the revision it was claimed at, the claimant's outcome write lands, and no second request is made after the claim is void. The rule is one helper, indexLiveClaim, which decide's live-claim branch and the back-fill's loop both call, so the two cannot drift.

proof.criterion: Review round 3, finding 2: the cursor's indexed field reaches only an older build that completes a sweep. One whose sweeps are all cut short (a SIGTERM in the pace wait, the cap of 300 requests, a rate limit) writes no cursor, so the marker stands and a record it created at its first claim, refused, with its attempt at the edge of Lookback, is read by nothing until the marker expires, which can be 72 hours.
proof.surface: The sweep against a real nats-server over a bucket holding a cursor this build wrote (indexed true), a marker older than Lookback, and an unlisted refused record with no entry and no Pending.
proof.observed: Passes at 30ceb42013e1. The marker now carries the moment its back-fill worked from, the sweep's own start, which is at or before the scan that read the records, so it never claims more cover than it had; a sweep back-fills again once that moment is further behind than Lookback, which is one whole-bucket read an hour at most. The cursor's indexed field is kept, so a roll-forward back-fills at once rather than within the hour.
proof.negativeControl: Run by the implementer, with any marker that exists counted fresh again: `--- FAIL: TestAMarkerOlderThanTheLookbackIsBackfilledAgain: guid-unlisted outcome "", want "redelivered"`.

openQuestions: None blocking. All 28 review threads are answered and resolved.
discoveredComplexity: A rule two readers of one bucket must both follow belongs in one helper the moment there are two of them. decide had the live-claim rule and its reason written out; the back-fill grew a second path to the same records and did not have it, and the cost was the claimant's own write. indexLiveClaim is now the one place that rule lives.

A marker that says work was done must say when, or it cannot say whether the work still holds. The index marker was a bare key, so the only thing that could bring the back-fill round again was the bucket's TTL expiring it; carrying the moment it was written turns it into a statement with an age, and the back-fill falls due against Lookback instead of 72 hours.

A signal read from what another build does not write only reaches a build that gets far enough to write. The cursor's indexed field reaches an older build that completes a sweep and no other, which is why it is kept for what it is good at - making a roll-forward immediate - and the marker's age carries the rest.
